name: AI agent delegation over A2A
description: Reference Trust Requirements Profile for an AI agent that hands work to other agents, or takes work from them, over A2A (the Agent2Agent protocol). It keeps every requirement of mcp-tool-checkpoint and adds two that the A2A adapter measures on the wire, one on the receipts a remote agent returns and one on the identity of an inbound caller. Illustrative draft values.

scope.intended_use: Trust requirements for one AI agent session that delegates tasks to remote agents over A2A or receives tasks from them.
scope.boundary: Every A2A delegation and inbound task in one agent session with the answer to each, and the tool calls in the same session with their results.
out_of_scope: The quality of a remote agent's answer
What a remote agent does inside its own session, which its own gate judges

scored_signals.reason: Runaway step counts point to loops or to a task the agent should hand back.
Repeated tool failures mean the agent is acting on broken information.
A burst of calls is how a looping agent burns money and hammers outside systems.
The volume of data an agent sends out of the session bounds what it can leak.

standing_bands.range: all signals within acceptable range and no hard rule met
one or more signals in the warning range
a signal in the critical range or a hard rule met

required_standing.source_requirement: The gate runs outside the agent and its model, so the agent cannot skip or edit its evidence.

notes: Threshold values are illustrative draft values.
Under the restricted response the gate allows reads and refuses writes, outbound calls, delegations and commands.
A halt stops the whole session until a person resets it. A review refuses only the call or withholds only the result in question.

unverified_receipts_refused is true when a remote agent's receipts fail verification and the deployment's policy sets receipt_mode to enforce. Under receipt_mode warn it stays false, and remote_receipts_verified records the failure.

anonymous_caller_refused is true when an inbound task carries no authenticated identity and the deployment's policy sets anonymous_callers to refuse. Under anonymous_callers allow it stays false, and caller_authenticated records the absence.
Secret and instruction detection matches published token formats and phrase patterns. Encoded or paraphrased content can pass it.
